title: Stairs for the drawing robot
instruction: The drawing robot drives over paper and draws a line behind it with a marker. Draw the target with the shortest program you can. Every command counts, including repeat and learn. Without repeating you won’t fit within the limit for a star: find the pattern that repeats and wrap it in a loop.

levels.goal: Stairs going up: four steps, each 30 high and 30 wide.
levels.hint: Draw one step: up, turn, straight on, turn back. How many times do those four commands repeat?
levels.why: The pattern is forward, right, forward, left. Repeat it 4×. Without a loop it would be 16 commands, with a loop 5.

levels.goal: A castle wall with battlements: four teeth 20 high and 20 wide, each followed by a gap of 20.
levels.target: opakuj 4 [ dopředu 20 vpravo 90 dopředu 20 vpravo 90 dopředu 20 vlevo 90 dopředu 20 vlevo 90 ]
levels.hint: One tooth and one gap are four lines and four turns. After the gap, the robot has to face the same way as at the start.
levels.why: The pattern is longer, eight commands, but it’s still just one. A loop only works if the robot ends up facing the same way as at the start: twice right and twice left cancel out. Without a loop it would be 32 commands.

levels.goal: A pyramid: three steps up and straight away three down, each step 20 high and 20 wide.
levels.target: opakuj 2 [ opakuj 3 [ dopředu 20 vpravo 90 dopředu 20 vlevo 90 ] vpravo 90 ]
levels.hint: One loop isn’t enough. Write a loop going up, then a turn and then a loop going down.
levels.why: Longer programs are made of several loops one after another: up, turn, down. And now the best part: the way down is the same pattern as the way up, just turned by 90°. If you notice that, you can wrap the loop in another loop and fit into 7 commands.

levels.goal: Stairs that grow: two steps 10 × 10, two steps 20 × 20 and two steps 30 × 30, one after another.
levels.target: nauč schody :s [ opakuj 2 [ dopředu :s vpravo 90 dopředu :s vlevo 90 ] ] schody 10 schody 20 schody 30
levels.hint: The three loops differ only in a number. Teach the robot a new command stairs and pass it the size of the step as the parameter :s.
levels.why: A procedure is a pattern with a variable: the same commands, a different number each time. Three loops one after another cost 15 commands, a procedure and three calls only 9. Programs for robots are built from exactly these small named pieces.

debrief: The robot can’t come up with the route. You can: you find the pattern and wrap it in a loop. The shorter the program, the fewer places for a mistake. That’s why the repeat block is used so often in MakeCode. And the first turtle of the Logo language really was a robot: it drove around on the floor and drew on paper with a pen.
